title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: JANELLE DRIVES
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Janelle Ortiz, a hospital cook in Tucson, Arizona.
She's thirty-one and has never driven a car. She takes three buses to work.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE THIRD BUS
segments.quote: To conquer fear is the beginning of wisdom.
segments.author: Bertrand Russell
lines: At seventeen, she backed her mom's car into a mailbox and quit for good.
One July day, her third bus broke down in one hundred and ten degrees.
A man at the stop read a line from Bertrand Russell:
To conquer fear is the beginning of wisdom.
Janelle walked to the DMV, dripping sweat, and got her learner's permit.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE CHURCH LOT
segments.quote: A small daily task, if it be really daily, will beat the labours of a spasmodic Hercules.
segments.author: Anthony Trollope
lines: Her neighbor Walt, a retired trucker, offered his old Buick.
Janelle wanted to be ready in a week. Walt tapped a line from Anthony Trollope on his dashboard:
A small daily task, if it be really daily, will beat the labours of a spasmodic Hercules.
So every evening, she drove slow circles in the church parking lot. Twenty minutes. Every day.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE ORANGE CONE
segments.quote: Only those who dare to fail greatly can ever achieve greatly.
segments.author: Robert F. Kennedy
lines: On her road test, she parked perfectly. Then she backed over an orange cone.
The examiner said, Ma'am, that cone had a family. She failed.
She cried in the Buick. Walt quoted Robert Kennedy:
Only those who dare to fail greatly can ever achieve greatly.
She booked the next test that afternoon.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE SECOND TRY
segments.quote: Patience is the companion of wisdom.
segments.author: Saint Augustine
lines: On the second test, a pickup honked behind her. Her hands shook.
She remembered her abuela's favorite line, from Saint Augustine:
Patience is the companion of wisdom.
She took one breath, waited her turn, and rolled through clean.
She passed. Walt leaned on the horn for a full minute.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE SLOW ROAD
segments.quote: Thanks to the Interstate Highway System, it is now possible to travel from coast to coast without seeing anything.
segments.author: Charles Kuralt
lines: Her abuela Chayo, eighty-four, had always wanted to see the Grand Canyon.
Janelle picked the interstate. Walt quoted Charles Kuralt, the old CBS reporter:
Thanks to the Interstate Highway System, it is now possible to travel from coast to coast without seeing anything.
So they took the slow roads and stopped for cherry pie.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE RIM
segments.quote: Leave it as it is. You cannot improve on it. The ages have been at work on it, and man can only mar it.
segments.author: Theodore Roosevelt
lines: At sunset, Janelle pushed Abuela's wheelchair to the rim.
Abuela whispered, Your grandpa promised me this. You did it.
A ranger told them what Theodore Roosevelt said there:
Leave it as it is. You cannot improve on it. The ages have been at work on it, and man can only mar it.
Janelle put her phone away and held Abuela's hand until the stars came out.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Face the fear. Practice daily. Dare to fail. Be patient. Take the slow road. Just look.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Face the fear. Practice daily. Dare to fail. Be patient. Take the slow road. And just look.
I learned to drive at sixteen. My dad's mailbox still hasn't forgiven me.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
